notes:
The whole of SFH 371 as held in the OAI-PMH harvest — 2,421 catalogue records, every one read. Agency photography of the redevelopment project areas, filed in eight series: Hunters Point A (558), Embarcadero-Lower Market / Golden Gateway E-1 (464), Western Addition A-1 and A-2 (411), Yerba Buena Center D-1 (411), Diamond Heights B-1 (365), General (180), Rincon Point-South Beach (14) and South of Market Earthquake Recovery (12). All 2,421 are rights-flagged No Copyright - United States.

Two things govern how it has to be read, and neither applies to SFP 23. First, the titles are narrative captions, not 'address, shop sign': '1249 Scott Street home on dolly being pulled by bulldozer'. The default business-name extraction returns caption prose and, worse, individuals at public ceremonies, so this collection runs under the extractor's named-buildings-only policy. Second, 234 records photograph people rather than places and carry no street number; they are skipped outright rather than kept as unresolved findings, because a record with no number can never become a page and keeping it would carry named individuals into the repository for nothing.

The dates are the strength here. 116 of 421 findings sit on a parcel, and much of what they show was cleared within a few years of the exposure - 1415 Scott Street and 1446-1454 Divisadero, photographed for a parcel appraisal on 10 August 1957, are two buildings on a block rebuilt as a single structure in 1963.

coverage.remaining: None. The collection was read whole; nothing in SFH 371 is outstanding.
coverage.note:
2,421 records read, 421 findings, 117 resolved to a parcel and 116 published on 103 pages; one declined because the page already carried six dated entries saying more. 49 of the published findings name the building standing at the address - overwhelmingly Tenderloin residential hotels (the Alton, Artmar, Columbia, Continental, Earle, Edgeworth, Herald, Iroquois, Jefferson, Jones, Kohlen, Lindy, Metro, Otis, Phillips, Roosevelt, Sweden, Windsor and Woodland among them), plus the Japantown YWCA, the Miyako Hotel, Woolf House Apartments, the Crocker Galleria, George Washington Carver Elementary School and the Western Addition Solar House.

304 unresolved, and the shape of that number is the point: 257 records give no street number at all (a view down a street, a model, a project-area overview), 33 name an address EAS no longer holds because the building was cleared, 6 name something the city's register does not treat as a street (Embarcadero Center, One Maritime Plaza, One Jackson Place, Ridgeview Terrace, Verona, and a 'W 24th Street' that is probably a cataloguing error), 5 are printed ranges now split across parcels, and 3 are condominiums. The 33 with no EAS record are the most valuable thing in the batch and the one class that cannot be published under the evidence bar - a dated photograph of a building at a number that no longer exists.
